BREAKING: The SDA has reached a proposed settlement in its national class action against ALDI over what the SDA contended is unpaid work performed before and after rostered shifts.

Including amounts previously paid by ALDI to some ALDI workers, the total value of the outcome is expected to be more than $50 million to approximately 32,000 current and former ALDI workers, subject to final calculations and approval by the Federal Court.

Work at KFC? Watch this update about the KFC Class Action now - you could be eligible for compensation if you worked at KFC between 25 October 2017 – 22 December 2023.

For SDA members, a secure home is getting harder to hold onto. 

More than half rent, and 71% don't own any property at all. Whether you're renting or trying to buy, the pressure is real: 62% spent more than 30% of their income on housing last year.

Everyone deserves a safe, affordable place to live, no matter what you earn. The SDA is doing the work to make that happen, backing renters' rights and pushing for more homes.
4 months ago today, we won our case to abolish junior rates at 18 years old... and honestly, we're still not over it 😅

SDA Victoria thanks @sallymcmanus1971 and @micheleoneilau for their remarkable contribution to working people and the Union movement. 

Their leadership helped drive real change, giving workers a stronger voice and delivering meaningful improvements to pay, rights and conditions.

They stood with SDA members in campaigns to Protect Penalty Rates, abolish junior rates for adults with Adult Age=Adult Wage and fight for Better Wages every year. 
We thank them for their dedication and wish them all the best for the future. @ausunions

Our campaign to Ban Aggressive Customers has reached a major milestone.
Workplace Protection Orders are now before Victorian Parliament.

No matter how big or powerful your employer is, you deserve to have the right to have a say on your pay and entitlements.

We’ve done just that at McDonald’s and Chemist Warehouse. But we’re not stopping there.
 
It’s time to strengthen these laws to make bargaining fairer, stronger and more accessible for Australian workers.
Workers shouldn’t have to wait years just to get the pay they’re owed.

The SDA is proud to support the Albanese Government’s announcement that it will create a new Fair Work Court to deal with workplace disputes and underpayments. 

It shouldn’t take several years for workers, like Sarah, to recover what they’re owed if they’re underpaid by their employer. 

A Fair Work Court will streamline this process, making it easier and quicker for workers to get back what they’re owed.

A SUPER win for young, Aussie workers 🎉 👇

Labor has announced a commitment to remove the 30 hour threshold so all working teenagers can receive super, regardless of the hours they’ve worked 👏😍

I, alongside the @sdaunion , have been advocating for this change for some time now and it’s such heartening news for young Aussie workers that work so hard for every dollar they earn 😍

The outdated under-18, 30-hour rule is on the way out 🚀

Labor is stepping up to support young people early in their working life so they can retire more comfortably at the other end ❤️

Today at the Labor Engaged Fringe during the ALP National Conference, the John Curtin Research Centre was proud to host the launch panel for Defending Australia: A National Artificial Intelligence Sovereign Capability and Security Agenda for the 21st Century.

A big thank you to The Hon. Chris Picton MP, Gerard Dwyer and Dr Dominic Meagher for an insightful discussion about one of the defining public policy challenges of our time.

Our conversation, moderated by our ED Nick @dyrenfurth, ranged from sovereign AI capability and national security to industrial strategy, critical infrastructure, democratic resilience and the future of work. A common theme emerged: artificial intelligence is no longer simply a technology issue. It is a question of economic sovereignty, national capability and ensuring Australia has the skills, institutions and industrial base to shape—not simply consume—the technologies that will define the decades ahead.

It was particularly fitting to hold this discussion in Adelaide, home to the world-leading Australian Institute for Machine Learning (AIML) and at the heart of Australia's growing defence, advanced manufacturing and innovation ecosystem.

Thank you to everyone who joined us and contributed to a lively audience discussion.

The conversation continues on Saturday morning at 8.00am, when we launch our latest report, Manufacturing Homes: A National Strategy for Solving Australia's Housing Crisis, with The Hon. Clare O'Neil MP, followed by a panel featuring Lachlan Kerwood-McCall, Tim Woods and Michael O'Connor. We look forward to seeing you there.
